outcomeNote: A dictum with two prooftexts and a reported practice with its verse; nothing is contested.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִיּוֹם שֶׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ נִנְעֲלוּ שַׁעֲרֵי תְּפִלָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״גַּם כִּי אֶזְעַק וַאֲשַׁוֵּעַ שָׂתַם תְּפִלָּתִי״. וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשַּׁעֲרֵי תְפִילָּה נִנְעֲלוּ, שַׁעֲרֵי דִמְעָה לֹא נִנְעֲלוּ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״שִׁמְעָה תְפִלָּתִי ה׳ וְשַׁוְעָתִי הַאֲזִינָה אֶל דִּמְעָתִי אַל תֶּחֱרַשׁ״.
segments.en: On the subject of prayer, «Rabbi Elazar also said: Since the day the Temple was destroyed the gates of prayer were locked» and prayer is not accepted as it once was, «as it is said» in lamentation of the Temple’s destruction: «“Though I plead and call out, He shuts out my prayer”» (Lamentations 3:8). Yet, «despite» the fact «that the gates of prayer were locked» with the destruction of the Temple, «the gates of tears were not locked,» and one who cries before God may rest assured that his prayers will be answered, «as it is stated: “Hear my prayer, Lord, and give ear to my pleading, keep not silence at my tears”» (Psalms 39:13). Since this prayer is a request that God should pay heed to the tears of one who is praying, he is certain that at least the gates of tears are not locked.

segments.he: רָבָא לָא גְּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא בְּיוֹמָא דְעֵיבָא, מִשּׁוּם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״סַכֹּתָה בֶעָנָן לָךְ מֵעֲבוֹר תְּפִלָּה״.
segments.en: With regard to the locking of the gates of prayer, the Gemara relates that «Rava did not decree a fast on a cloudy day because it is stated: “You have covered Yourself in a cloud, through which prayer cannot pass”» (Lamentations 3:44). The verse indicates that clouds are a bad omen, indicating that God has averted His face (Rav Hai Gaon).

moves.cueHe: ואמר רבי אלעזר: מיום שחרב בית המקדש ננעלו שערי תפלה
moves.summary: R' Elazar: since the Temple's destruction the gates of prayer are locked.
moves.about: the lament 'He shuts out my prayer' as proof that the gates of prayer were locked with the destruction

moves.cueHe: שנאמר: ״גם כי אזעק ואשוע שתם תפלתי״
moves.summary: Proof from Lamentations 3:8, 'He shuts out my prayer'.
moves.about: 'keep not silence at my tears' as proof that the gates of tears were not locked

moves.cueHe: ואף על פי ששערי תפילה ננעלו, שערי דמעה לא ננעלו
moves.summary: Qualification of the first ruling: though the gates of prayer are locked, the gates of tears are not.

moves.cueHe: שנאמר: ״שמעה תפלתי ה׳ ושועתי האזינה אל דמעתי אל תחרש״
moves.summary: Proof from Psalms 39:13, whose plea rests on God heeding tears.

moves.cueHe: רבא לא גזר תעניתא ביומא דעיבא
moves.summary: On the theme of locked gates of prayer, the gemara reports that Rava did not decree a fast on a cloudy day.
moves.about: Rava did not decree a fast on a cloudy day

moves.cueHe: משום שנאמר ״סכתה בענן לך מעבור תפלה״
moves.summary: The reason: Lamentations 3:44, 'You have covered Yourself in a cloud, through which prayer cannot pass'.
moves.about: 'You have covered Yourself in a cloud, through which prayer cannot pass' as the reason for not decreeing a fast on a cloudy day
